In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Alps have not only a geosynclinal, but also a tectonically controlled origin.
the Alps and the Carpathian Mountains are the result of the collision between the African and Eurasian plates.

the Alpine Orogen is a mountain chain, which is the product of a geosynclinal development, and which is still under the control of the same geotectonic factors that were active in the pre-alpine period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Alpine orogeny has been a process of long duration (about 10 m. yr.) and of great horizontal extension (about 500 km).

the present end-stage of the Alpine-Carpathian orogen is the result of a time- and space-controlled process which took place over a horizontal distance of more than 500 km during approximately 10 million years.
the Alpine orogeny is a complex process, which is not only characterized by a long lasting and intensive tectonics but also by the development of a complex and diversified geology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Alpine orogeny is a long-term process, which has been going on for about 50 Myr.
the Alpine-Karpathian orogenic belt is a large-scale structure which developed over a horizontal distance of more than 500 km and in a period of 10 m.y.

the Alpine-Carpathian-Auvergne orogen is a 500 km-wide belt that developed over 10 million years, with its northern margin being consolidated in a NE direction at a rate of about 50 km/Myr (Section I).
